catalog_citation: Temple, O. (ed. C. L. Temple). 1922. Notes on the Tribes, Provinces, Emirates and States of the Northern Provinces of Nigeria, compiled from official reports. 2nd ed. Lagos: C.M.S. Bookshop (Glottolog cites the Cape Town: Argus printing; 1st ed. 1919; repr. London: Cass 1965). Entry 'Auyokawa, Shirawa, Teshenawa', pp.32-34 (authorities: Capt. J. M. Fremantle, Mr. K. L. Hall).
catalog_locator: p.33 (2nd ed. 1922; identical text 1st ed. 1919 p.33 of archive.org notesontribespro00temp)
catalog_quote: Native authority claims that the Auyokawa are of the same stock as the Bedde, originating from a town called Badr, east of Bagirimi. The two languages show close resemblance, the termination of nouns and a strong accentuation of the last syllable being very noticeable. Many of the words are identical. Auyokanchi is, however, now spoken only by two old men.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Impressionistic colonial-administrative remark: in Auyokanchi (and Bade) 'a strong accentuation of the last syllable' is very noticeable, i.e. perceived word-final prominence.
new_statements.identity_note: Entry is explicitly about the Auyokawa of Auyo/Auweya, Hadeija Emirate (Kano Province), 'of the same stock as the Bedde', language 'Auyokanchi.. now spoken only by two old men' -- matches Migeod's 1920s report of two remaining Awiaka speakers; = auyo1240. The accent remark is made jointly of 'the two languages' (Auyokanchi and Bedde/Bade).

sources.citation: Schuh, Russell G. 2001. Shira, Teshena, Auyo: Hausa's (former) eastern neighbors. In Derek Nurse (ed.), Historical Language Contact in Africa (Sprache und Geschichte in Afrika 16/17), 387-435. Köln: Rüdiger Köppe.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Sec. 3.1 p.399: the only Auyo data known is Migeod's (1924:320) short 'Awiaka' list = numerals 1-10, tens 20-100, Arabic day names, one phrase (reproduced in Appendix I, p.429); p.402: Harris and Migeod 'did not mark tone or vowel length'. Sec. 3.2 treats segmental sound changes and numerals only; Bade/Ngizim comparanda are tone-marked, Auyo forms are not.
